P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Not established. The Bank of the Republic of Burundi (BRB) adopted a new foreign-exchange regulation in December 2023 (per IMF summaries), and exporters' foreign receipts have been subject to repatriation rules; the rules for individual service exporters were not captured.
P1_fx_receipts.note: IMF Q&A page 403 to snapshot tool; no BRB regulation text captured on 2026-10-22.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Burundi (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Lemon Squeezy payouts; Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Companies are created at the one-stop shop (Guichet Unique de Création des Entreprises) within the investment promotion agency, set up by an order of 31 Jan 2013, which lists company forms (single-member, SPRL, SA, cooperatives). The sole-trader route and fees were not confirmed.
L1_registration.note: Single secondary domain (creerentreprise.fr) on 2026-10-22; API official page not captured.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 18% (10% for defined categories; 0% for qualifying exports and international transport). The Budget Law 2026/27 (Loi n° 1/10 of 30 June 2026) cut the compulsory registration threshold from BIF 100m to BIF 25m, with an optional threshold of BIF 5m, from 1 July 2026. Whether exported services qualify for 0% was not confirmed.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The National Assembly unanimously adopted a personal data protection bill on 15 January 2026. It creates an independent administrative authority and sets several protection regimes. Senate passage, promulgation and entry into force were not confirmed.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed). The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
